# AI Monoculture in the Stock Market: Do LLM-Generated Trading Agents Converge?

Code, generated agents and results for the research paper of the same name.

**Question.** Do trading agents independently generated by the same large language model (LLM) converge more than chance, and does mixing providers reduce it?

**Design.** 30 trading agents each were generated by Claude Sonnet 5, Gemini 3.6 Flash and GPT-5.6 Terra from the same open prompt (`prompt.txt`). Every agent was run on 30-minute bars for 486 S&P 500 stocks (2024 warm-up, 2025 scored) and compared with 30 random and 30 popular comparison agents on holdings overlap (Jaccard, cosine, weighted Jaccard), trading direction (flow imbalance) and crowding (effective number of stocks).

**Headline results.**
- Same-model agents overlapped more than different-model agents (Jaccard 0.189 vs 0.129), and all AI agents overlapped far more than chance (random agents 0.012).
- GPT showed the strongest model-specific style, Claude a partial one, Gemini none (permutation tests, 5,000 shuffles).
- Mixing providers removed only about a third of the excess overlap (diversification floor 66%, 95% CI 55-76%) and almost none of the one-sided trading.

## What is in this repository

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `prompt.txt` | The exact prompt sent to every model |
| `universe.txt` | The 503 S&P 500 tickers as of January 2024 |
| `agents/` | All 90 generated agents: code (`.py`), full model response (`.raw.txt`) and generation settings (`.meta.json`). Claude agents are named `agent_NNN`, Gemini `gemini_NNN`, GPT `gpt_NNN` |
| `runs.tar.gz` | Every agent's recorded orders (`trades.csv`) and run status (`run.json`), including the 60 comparison agents. Extract with `tar xzf runs.tar.gz` |
| `report/csv/` | Every result table used in the paper |
| `report/figures/` | Every figure |

Market data is **not** included: Alpaca data cannot be redistributed. `fetch_tape.py` recreates the exact dataset.

## Scripts

| Script | What it does |
|---|---|
| `fetch_tape.py` | Downloads 30-minute SIP bars (2024-2025) for the universe from Alpaca |
| `rebuild.py` | Applies the coverage filter (stocks with a bar in at least 99% of timestamps, leaving 486) |
| `generate.py`, `generate_gemini.py`, `generate_openai.py` | Generate agents: one API call each, prompt sent verbatim, no system prompt |
| `harness.py` | Runs one agent bar by bar; the agent only ever sees data up to the current bar |
| `score.py` | Replays orders under the fill rules to rebuild holdings; behaviour stats and pairwise overlap |
| `baseline.py` | Builds the random and popular comparison agents |
| `report.py` | Main analysis: overlap, permutation tests, flow imbalance, regimes, clustering, figures |
| `floor.py` | Diversification floor with agent-level bootstrap (2,000 resamples) |
| `crowd.py` | Group-level overlap and effective number of stocks, including mixed 10+10+10 crowds |
| `flow_mixed.py` | Flow imbalance for size-matched mixed groups |
| `timeline.py` | Per-bar Jaccard through 2025 (Figure 1) |
| `power.py` | Power analysis with simulated agents |
| `checks.py` | Robustness checks (crashed agent, fill rates, convergence ratio) |
| `arrows.py` | Portfolio "arrow" and cosine heatmap figure |
| `analyze.py`, `null.py` | Earlier analysis helpers (strategy classification, standalone null test) |

## Reproducing the results

Python 3.11. Install dependencies:

```
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

API keys go in a file called `keys.txt` next to the scripts (it is in `.gitignore`; never commit it):

```
KEY=your_alpaca_key
SECRET=your_alpaca_secret
ANTHROPIC=your_anthropic_key
GOOGLE=your_google_key
OPENAI=your_openai_key
```

Then:

```
# 1. market data
python3 fetch_tape.py
python3 rebuild.py 0.99

# 2. agents (optional: the 90 agents used in the paper are already in agents/)
python3 generate.py --n 30
python3 generate_gemini.py --n 30
python3 generate_openai.py --n 30

# 3. run every agent (or extract runs.tar.gz to skip this step)
for f in agents/*.py; do python3 harness.py "$f" --timeout 60; done

# 4. comparison agents
python3 baseline.py --n 30 --match runs/*
python3 baseline.py --n 30 --mode weighted --match runs/* --prefix popular

# 5. analysis
python3 report.py all runs/*
python3 floor.py --boot 2000
python3 crowd.py runs/*
python3 flow_mixed.py runs/*
python3 timeline.py runs/* --smooth 5
python3 power.py
python3 checks.py
```

Outputs go to `report/csv/` and `report/figures/`.

## AI use

The trading agents studied here were generated by the three LLMs as the subject of the experiment. Separately, an AI assistant (Claude, Anthropic) helped write the analysis code and develop the statistical methods, under the author's direction. See the AI-use statement in the paper.
